          ADDM Report for Task 'ADDM:938362223_1_17035'

Analysis Period

AWR snapshot range from 17034 to 17035.
Time period starts at 06-SEP-25 11.30.53 AM
Time period ends at 06-SEP-25 12.30.01 PM

Analysis Target

Database 'MERCURY' with DB ID 938362223.
Database version during analysis period was 19.25.0.0.0.
Database version when ADDM was executed was 19.0.0.0.0.
All recommendations generated by ADDM are valid for database version 19.0.0.0.0, the version in which ADDM was executed.
ADDM performed an analysis of instance mercury, numbered 1 and hosted at
merc-dbpr.

Activity During the Analysis Period
-----------------------------------
Total database time was 28530 seconds.
The average number of active sessions was 8.04.

Summary of Findings
-------------------
    Description                      Active Sessions      Recommendations
                                     Percent of Activity
    -------------------------------  -------------------  ---------------
1   Session Connect and Disconnect   2.54 | 31.62         1

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 2.54 active sessions, 31.62% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 2.54 active sessions, 31.62% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.21 active sessions, 15.11% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.21 active sessions, 15.11% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.21 active sessions, 15.11% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "500" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 3: Unusual "Other" Wait Event
Impact is 1.09 active sessions, 13.54% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Wait event "Failed Logon Delay" in wait class "Other" was consuming
significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.09 active sessions, 13.54% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "Failed Logon Delay" waits. Refer to
      Oracle's "Database Reference" for the description of this wait event.

   Recommendation 2: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.09 active sessions, 13.54% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "Failed Logon Delay" waits in Module
      "oracle@merc-dbpr".

   Recommendation 3: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.09 active sessions, 13.54% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "Failed Logon Delay" waits in Service
      "SYS$USERS".

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Other" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.28 active sessions, 15.89% of total activity.


Finding 4: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .33 active sessions, 4.16% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .33 active sessions, 4.16% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .68 active sessions, 8.48% of total activity.


Finding 5: Top SQL Statements
Impact is .3 active sessions, 3.78% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .3 active sessions, 3.78% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "56980hjqxb68r" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 56980hjqxb68r.
         BEGIN PKG_COMMON_PROC.PROC_SETENV(:1,:2); END;
   Rationale
      The SQL Tuning Advisor cannot operate on PL/SQL statements.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 3% for SQL execution,
      26% for parsing, 71% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java execution.


Finding 6: Commits and Rollbacks
Impact is .26 active sessions, 3.24% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Waits on event "log file sync" while performing COMMIT and ROLLBACK operations
were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .26 active sessions, 3.24% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the possibility of improving the performance of I/O to the
      online redo log files.
   Rationale
      The average size of writes to the online redo log files was 12 K and the
      average time per write was 0 milliseconds.
   Rationale
      The total I/O throughput on redo log files was 4.2 M per second for
      reads and 8.6 M per second for writes.
   Rationale
      The redo log I/O throughput was divided as follows: 0% by RMAN and
      recovery, 67% by Log Writer, 0% by Archiver, 0% by Streams AQ and 32% by
      all other activity.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Commit" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .26 active sessions, 3.24% of total activity.


Finding 7: Java Execution
Impact is .16 active sessions, 2.03% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
JAVA execution consumed significant database time.

   No recommendations are available.


Finding 8: Unusual "Other" Wait Event
Impact is .16 active sessions, 2.01% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Wait event "OJVM: Generic" in wait class "Other" was consuming significant
database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .16 active sessions, 2.01% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action

      "Database Reference" for the description of this wait event.

   Recommendation 2: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .16 active sessions, 2.01% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "OJVM: Generic" waits in Service
